hero.title: Where can I take your product?
hero.lede: Software engineer at IBM. I ship production web apps and the services behind them, and I teach people how they work.
hero.imageCaption: Drop a golden-hour photo: Moroccan coast or Atlas mountains

stops.body: Five years of computer engineering at EMSI, finished in 2023. Algorithms, databases, networks, plus the habit of shipping a working project every semester instead of a slide deck.
Built an e-commerce site in Django: catalogue, cart, orders, admin. It was the first time my code had to deal with real users and real edge cases.
A finance application on Spring Boot with an Angular front end. Learned how a typed API contract keeps two teams from arguing.

Software engineer on enterprise products. I build the services behind them and the apps on top, and I maintain several of them in production. I design and document the features I ship, review code, pair with the team, mentor juniors, and run client demos.

items.title: Airline & travel web apps
items.desc: Sole maintainer of multiple production Angular apps, carried from v14 to v18. Booking flows, deep linking, interactive maps, real-time status tracking, and a multilingual UI that switches language at runtime. State in NgRx/RxJS; data over GraphQL and REST via AWS Amplify.
items.imageCaption: abstract airline booking-flow mockup, boarding-pass motif

items.title: Operations center dashboard
items.desc: A real-time decision-support hub for a US utilities company. It pulls operational KPIs from several systems into one screen operators can read at a glance during an incident.

items.title: Energy Data Hub
items.desc: A data platform for utilities. Teams get their own workspaces, build data flows on a drag-and-drop canvas, and follow them on live metrics dashboards. Grid models are converted to the CIM standard and processed on AWS with Lambda, Step Functions and Kafka, behind role-based access in Cognito.
items.imageCaption: abstract energy data hub mockup: turbines, solar, power grid

items.title: My Mini Souq
items.desc: A shop split into services: discovery, gateway, and typed service-to-service calls. I built it to work through the microservices pattern end to end, it isn't a real store.

items.title: OpenAI Q&A API
items.desc: A Java service that sends a question to an LLM, stores the answer, and hands it back over a clean REST endpoint.

items.title: JWT Spring Security
items.desc: A token-based auth setup, built the way I wish tutorials explained it: one filter chain you can actually follow.

items.title: Rojesty
items.desc: A decision-support dashboard for project managers: import the numbers, get the charts that answer "are we late?".

items.title: Expense Tracker
items.desc: An expense tracker split in two: an Angular front end for entering and reviewing spending, and a JEE back end holding the accounts and totals.

items.title: EBanking
items.desc: An online banking app: an Angular client talking to a Spring Boot microservices backend for accounts, operations, and balances.

darija.title: Java explained in Darija
darija.desc: Lambdas, Comparator, Predicate, Consumer, inner classes: explained in the language my students actually think in, because a few of them pick up Java faster in Darija than in English.

teaching.note: At IBM I mentor juniors and run client demos. Explaining a system out loud is half my job, and it is the same thing I do in a lesson.

answers.text: She maintains production Angular apps at IBM and has carried them from v14 through v18, including the migration work that comes with each major version: standalone components, new control flow, and dependency churn.
Yes. She teaches code reading, Java/Spring, Angular, Python and interview prep 1-on-1, mentors interns at IBM, and publishes a "Java explained in Darija" series aimed at beginners.
She is open to contract work now, based in Casablanca (GMT+1), which overlaps European hours fully and US East mornings. Replies within 24 hours.
Backend is Java/Spring (Boot, Cloud, Eureka, Gateway, OpenFeign, Security), plus Python: Django apps and AWS Lambda@Edge functions in production.
CI/CD with GitHub Workflows and Bitbucket Pipelines, AWS Amplify for GraphQL/REST data, and Lambda@Edge in Python. She also owns a shared UI library used across teams.
Arabic native, English TOEFL 91, French C1. She leads client demos in English and French.
AWS Certified AI Practitioner (2026), watsonx Code Assistant (2024), IBM Technical Advocate Cloud v4 (2023), Azure Fundamentals (2023).
Her IBM work is for airline and travel clients; names are withheld under NDA. The work itself: booking flows, interactive maps, real-time status tracking, multilingual UI.
